answer:
OCR/import issues are a major operational bottleneck that directly degrades onboarding performance and contributes to support load.

- Scanned, image-only PDFs lack a text layer, so the citation engine cannot produce reliable links; without OCR, citation accuracy drops and customers fail the go-live quality threshold [NL-015#NL-015-S04].
- During ingestion, such documents cause failed ingestion, incomplete text extraction, low-quality or missing TutorChat answers, and require manual OCR pre-processing that adds weeks to onboarding—e.g., Northstar Financial’s pilot was delayed three weeks [NL-010#NL-010-S06].
- OCR processing accounts for 25% of onboarding delay incidents and can produce the longest onboardings, as with BrightPath Healthcare at 9.5 weeks due to scanned PDF compliance issues [NL-012#NL-012-S06], [NL-031#NL-031-S04].
- OCR/scanned-PDF problems cause incomplete citations that fail the 85% citation correctness validation threshold, triggering the mandatory remediation path and possible escalation [NL-031#NL-031-S04], [NL-005#NL-005-S11].
- Import/OCR queue issues can also affect overall system performance—the March 14 outage was caused by an import worker retry storm, and OCR batches can block fast uploads, requiring split-queue architecture [NL-021#NL-021-S06].
- Recurring blockers such as OCR/import issues are reviewed monthly against onboarding metrics and support ticket patterns, linking them to both onboarding outcomes and support workload [NL-005#NL-005-S11].
